title: Version-gated runtime behavior flags and replayable contract test harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a safe, observable way to introduce behavioral changes to the core Text/Chat API (streaming semantics, function-calling shape, and structured output enforcement) while preserving customers' existing contracts. Changes to runtime behavior have historically caused subtle regressions for streaming clients and tool-call integrations.

Goal: Implement server-side, version-gated behavior flags plus a replayable contract test harness that can replay historical production traffic against candidate runtime behaviors to detect regressions before rollout. The ticket covers API surface for version headers, runtime gating, test harness infra, CI integration, and monitoring/rollback signals.
acceptance_criteria: All runtime behavior changes must be controllable by a version header and by a server-side flag with deterministic evaluation.

A replay harness exists that can take exported request traces (streaming and non-streaming) and replay them reproducibly against the current and candidate behaviors; diffs are automatically computed and surfaced.
CI job runs the backward-compatibility suite on every PR touching runtime or API surface; failures block merges when regressions exceed predefined thresholds.
Telemetry dashboards show per-route divergence rates (structured-output schema violations, tool-call arg mismatches, streaming chunk differences) with alerting rules tied to rollout percentage.
A documented rollback policy and automated safeguard (automatic throttling/fallback to previous behavior version) are wired into the runtime.

Integration tests covering: streaming reassembly, mid-stream function-call initiation, KV-cache re-usage across continuations, and structured-output schema enforcement run reliably in CI under multiple version gates.
implementation_plan: Design and expose an optional client 'X-Redwood-Behavior-Version' header; default remains legacy behavior.
Add server-side 'behavior_gate' registry: each behavior has: id, description, stable_version, rollout_percentage, and compatibility_test_matrix tags.
Implement deterministic evaluation path that reads header, overrides rollout, and logs gate decisions to tracing/span metadata.

Build a replay engine: canonicalize incoming trace (preserve token-level events, tool-calls, function-call handshakes, and streaming boundaries), and execute them against candidate behavior implementations in an isolated test env.
Create a comparator that validates structured-output against JSON Schema/Shape rules and emits categorized diffs (schema_violation, content_mismatch, timing_mismatch).
Add CI matrix that replays a sample corpus (golden prompts + anonymized production traces) for each PR label 'runtime' and fails on threshold breaches.
Instrument dashboards and SLO alarms for divergence signals; integrate with runbooks for on-call fallback.
Ship SDK changes (docs + minor header helpers) and quickstart migration guide for customers who want to opt into new behavior early.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dogfood: enable header opt-in for internal services and run replay harness on 72h trace window. Monitor divergence metrics.
Phase 1 - Beta customers: invite 3 integration partners to opt-in to behavior header; run replays daily and collect customer feedback.
Phase 2 - Gradual public rollout: start server-side rollout at 1% per-region with automatic check of divergence > threshold to pause progress.
Phase 3 - Full migration: when divergence stable < threshold for 14 days and key regressions resolved, flip default header to new stable_version and keep legacy gate for 90 days before removal.
Rollback: automatic server-side rollback when schema-violation rate > 0.5% or token-level latency increase > 20% for a sustained 10-minute window.
telemetry_and_metrics: metric: runtime.behavior_gate.divergence_rate{route,gate_id} - percent of requests with comparator diffs
metric: runtime.behavior_gate.streaming_reseq_failures{route,gate_id} - reassembly mismatches for streaming clients
alert: divergence_high - fires when divergence_rate > 0.2% sustained for 5m during rollout
dashboard: per-route drift table with sample request diffs and links to anonymized replay traces
test_cases: Streaming continuity: replay token-level stream with delayed chunks and assert final concatenated output equals golden response under both behaviors.
Mid-stream function-call: replay scenario where an assistant initiates a function call halfway through a stream; ensure call payload shape and tool-call ordering preserved.
Structured output schema: run JSON Schema validation against structured output variants and classify violations as major/minor.
Backward regression matrix: run the replay corpus across previous three runtime versions and candidate change; expect zero critical regressions.
KV cache reuse: replay repeated prefixes and measure token savings; assert cache semantics unchanged between versions.
